advances: Requires actual $C^2$ cap integrals and contact minimum. It neither supplies them at an arbitrary extremizer nor asserts a sign for the coupled objective.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The homogeneous Jacobian equations in the threshold and common-mass unknowns are $-S_j\,db_j-dq=0$ and $\sum_j\rho_j\,db_j=0$. They force $B\,dq=0$, hence all increments vanish. The implicit function theorem gives the unique nearby branch. At every mark the weighted sum of actual through-mark thresholds is at least the equalized sum; at least one actual threshold is at least its equalized threshold. The cap integral is nonincreasing in its threshold, so the corresponding through-mark cap has mass at most $q(t)$. This argument uses the minimum over the actual deformed fiber and does not give a comparison on unselected fibers.

Differentiate once to get $q'=F_{j,t}-S_jr_j$. Differentiate twice to get $q''=K_j-S_jb_j''(0)$ and sum $b_j''(0)=(K_j-q'')/S_j$ with weights $\rho_j$, giving the formula. On a fixed-width planar patch the contribution to $K_j$ is the second derivative along the linear threshold path $b_j+t r_j$, with distance velocity $r_j/\|u_j\|$ for fixed continuous covector $u_j$. Thus the negative of its contribution is the corresponding signed slab curvature when its differentiability hypotheses hold. Any changing width $h\Gamma_t(u_j)$ must be included in the actual partial derivatives. No one patch controls the sign of $q''$ before the other partial terms and $\alpha''$ are included. The formula does not control those remaining terms uniformly along changing bodies or imply the $C^2$ hypotheses for an outward ramp at kink traces.

For the local variable-width calculation, let $J$ be the primitive of the smoothing CDF $\Psi$ as in the planar slab integrals, and write $w=h\Gamma_t>0$, $s$ for the signed margin at the moving integration endpoint, and $k=s/w$. Where the derivative exists and the relevant functions are twice differentiable,
$$
(wJ(k))''=w''(J(k)-k\Psi(k))+s''\Psi(k)+\frac{\Psi'(k)}{w}(s'-kw')^2.
$$
This follows by differentiating $(wJ(k))'=w'(J(k)-k\Psi(k))+s'\Psi(k)$. For fixed bounded velocities, bounded $\Psi'(k)$ and $k$, and a $C^2$ scale $\Gamma_t$ bounded below away from zero with bounded derivatives, the cross term from $w'=h\Gamma_t'$ is bounded as $h\downarrow0$, while the square of $s'$ is multiplied by $1/(h\Gamma_t)$. This is a local primitive computation; saturation must be maintained at the remote endpoint and it yields no global remainder bound.
statement:
Along an actual scalar body path, let $F_j(t,b)$ be the raw mass of its $j$-th fixed-normal smoothed cap at threshold $b$. Assume $F_j$ is $C^2$ near $(0,b_j)$, $F_j(0,b_j)=Q$, and $S_j=-F_{j,b}(0,b_j)>0$. Fix $\rho_j>0$ with $\sum_j\rho_j=1$. Let $\tau_j(t,Y)$ denote the actual through-mark threshold for mark $Y$ in the deformed source fiber, with any prescribed mark-dependent buffer included, and assume the contact minimum $\alpha(t)=\min_Y\sum_j\rho_j[\tau_j(t,Y)-b_j]$ is $C^2$ and $\alpha(0)=0$. Then the system $F_j(t,b_j(t))=q(t)$ and $\sum_j\rho_j(b_j(t)-b_j)=\alpha(t)$ has a unique nearby $C^2$ branch and supplies a cap depth upper bound $q(t)$ at every mark on that source fiber. Writing $r_j=b_j'(0)$, $B=\sum_j\rho_j/S_j$ and $K_j=F_{j,tt}+2r_jF_{j,tb}+r_j^2F_{j,bb}$ at $(0,b_j)$,
$$
q''(0)=\frac{\sum_j\rho_j K_j/S_j-\alpha''(0)}{B}.
$$
title: The second derivative of an equalized actual smoothed cap cover
